nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
nodes.statement: For any set of $n$ points $x_1,\dots,x_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, there exists a map $f:\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^m$ with $m=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ such that $(1-\varepsilon)\|x_i-x_j\|_2 \le \|f(x_i)-f(x_j)\|_2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|x_i-x_j\|_2$ for all $i,j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Random linear projection to dimension $O(\log n / \varepsilon^2)$ approximately preserves all pairwise Euclidean distances within $(1\pm\varepsilon)$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ and $(p,q)$ bilinear form
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ is $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=p+q$) with bilinear form $\langle u,v\rangle = \sum_{i=1}^p u_i v_i - \sum_{i=p+1}^{p+q} u_i v_i = u^T \Lambda v$, where $\Lambda = \mathrm{diag}(+1,\dots,+1,-1,\dots,-1)$ has $p$ ones and $q$ minus-ones.
nodes.statement_clean: Vector space with an indefinite inner product of signature $(p,q)$.

nodes.name: $(p,q)$-norm and interval square
nodes.statement: For $v \in \mathbb{R}^{p,q}$, the scalar square is $\langle v,v \rangle$ and the squared $(p,q)$-norm is $\|v\|_{p,q}^2 = \langle v,v\rangle$. The interval square between $u,v$ is $\langle u-v,u-v\rangle = \|u-v\|_{p,q}^2$.

nodes.name: Symmetric hollow dissimilarity matrix
nodes.statement: An $n\times n$ matrix $D$ with $D_{ij} = D_{ji}$ (symmetric) and $D_{ii}=0$ (hollow); the triangle inequality is NOT required.

nodes.name: Gram matrix $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$ via centering
nodes.statement: For symmetric hollow $D$, define $\mathrm{Gram}(D) = -CDC/2$ with centering matrix $C = I - \tfrac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}_n \mathbf{1}_n^T$.

nodes.name: Generalized power distance
nodes.statement: For two balls centered at $p,q \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with radii $r_p, r_q$, $\mathrm{Pow}((p,r_p),(q,r_q)) = \|p-q\|_E^2 - (r_p+r_q)^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Squared length of the internal tangent segment between two disjoint balls; reduces to squared Euclidean distance when $r_p=r_q=0$.

nodes.name: Power of a point (classical)
nodes.statement: The power of point $p$ with respect to a circle centered at $q$ with radius $r$ is $\|p-q\|^2 - r^2$.

nodes.name: Silhouette coefficient
nodes.statement: For point $x \in X$, $a(x)$ is the average distance from $x$ to other points in $X$, $b(x)$ the average distance from $x$ to points in cluster $Y$; $\bar s(x) = (b(x)-a(x))/\mathrm{Norm}(a(x),b(x))$, and the cluster silhouette is the average over $x \in X$.

nodes.name: Unnormalized silhouette score $SC_W$ between two Gaussians
nodes.statement: $SC_W(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y}) \triangleq \mathrm{DIS}^2_W(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y}) - (\Delta[\mathcal{X}]+\Delta[\mathcal{Y}])$, where $\mathrm{DIS}_W$ is the 2-Wasserstein distance and $\Delta[\mathcal{X}] = \mathbb{E}_{x,x'\sim\mathcal{X}}[\|x-x'\|^2]$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-Euclidean representation of any symmetric hollow matrix
nodes.statement: For any hollow symmetric matrix $D$, there is a symmetric bilinear form $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{p,q}$ with integers $p,q$ and $n$ vectors $x_1,\dots,x_n$ such that $D_{ij} = \langle x_i-x_j, x_i-x_j\rangle$.
conclusions: $\exists\, p,q$ with $p+q=n$ and $x_1,\dots,x_n$ such that $D_{ij} = \langle x_i-x_j, x_i-x_j\rangle_{p,q}$

nodes.name: Pseudo-Euclidean JL with additive Euclidean error (Lemma 2.2)
nodes.statement: For any $n$ points $x_1,\dots,x_n \in \mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exists $f:\mathbb{R}^{p,q}\to\mathbb{R}^{p',q'}$ with $p',q'=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ such that $\|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2 - \varepsilon\|x_i-x_j\|_E^2 \le \|f(x_i)-f(x_j)\|_{p',q'}^2 \le \|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2 + \varepsilon\|x_i-x_j\|_E^2$.
conclusions: $\exists f:\mathbb{R}^{p,q}\to\mathbb{R}^{p',q'}$ with $p',q'=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ such that $\|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2 \pm \varepsilon\|x_i-x_j\|_E^2$ bounds hold

nodes.name: Fine-grained JL lemma in pseudo-Euclidean space (Theorem 2.3)
nodes.statement: For any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exists $f:\mathbb{R}^{p,q}\to\mathbb{R}^{p',q'}$ with $p',q'=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ such that $(1-\varepsilon C_{ij})\|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2 \le \|f(x_i)-f(x_j)\|_{p',q'}^2 \le (1+\varepsilon C_{ij})\|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2$, where $C_{ij} = \|x_i-x_j\|_E^2 / \|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2$.
conclusions: $\exists f$ to dimension $p'+q'=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ with multiplicative distortion at most $1\pm\varepsilon C_{ij}$

nodes.name: Bounded ratio of $(p,q)$-norm and Euclidean norm (Lemma 2.4)
nodes.statement: Let $v \in \mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ with each coordinate sampled from a distribution $f$ with finite second moment. With high probability, $\|v\|_E^2 < C\|v\|_{p,q}^2$ if $q < \tfrac{C-1}{C+1} p$, or $\|v\|_E^2 < -C\|v\|_{p,q}^2$ if $p < \tfrac{C-1}{C+1} q$, for $C>1$.
assumptions: $v \in \mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ with i.i.d. coordinates from distribution $f$ with finite second moment

nodes.name: Bounded norm ratio for uniform unit-sphere vector (Corollary 2.5)
nodes.statement: A random vector $v$ chosen uniformly on $S^{p+q-1}$ has, with high probability, $\|v\|_E^2 < C\|v\|_{p,q}^2$ whenever $q < \tfrac{C-1}{C+1} p$.

nodes.name: JL with $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ distortion for random points in $(p,q)$-space (Theorem 2.6)
nodes.statement: Let $X \subset \mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ be randomly selected of size $n$ with $q<\tfrac{C-1}{C+1}p$ for constant $C$, with $(u-v)/\|u-v\|_E$ uniform on $S^{p+q-1}$. With high probability there exists $f:\mathbb{R}^{p,q}\to\mathbb{R}^{p',q'}$, $p',q'=O(C^2 \log(n)/\varepsilon^2)$, such that $(1-\varepsilon)\|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2 \le \|f(x_i)-f(x_j)\|_{p',q'}^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2$.
conclusions: w.h.p. $\exists f$ with target dim $O(C^2\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ achieving $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ multiplicative distortion of $\|\cdot\|_{p,q}^2$

nodes.name: Symmetric hollow matrices as power distance matrices (Lemma 3.1)
nodes.statement: Given any $n\times n$ symmetric hollow $D$, we can write $D = E + 4r^2(I-J)$ with $r\in\mathbb{R}_+$, $E$ a Euclidean distance matrix, $I$ identity, $J=\mathbf{1}_n\mathbf{1}_n^T$. Moreover $E$ is Euclidean iff $2r^2 \ge |e_n|$ where $e_n$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$.
conclusions: $\exists r \in \mathbb{R}_+$ such that $D = E + 4r^2(I-J)$ with $E$ a Euclidean distance matrix iff $2r^2 \ge |e_n|$

nodes.name: JL for generalized power distance (Lemma 3.2)
nodes.statement: Given $n$ weighted points $(p_i,r_i)$ with $p_i\in\mathbb{R}^d$, there exists $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^m$ with $m=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ such that for all $i\ne j$, $(1-\varepsilon)\mathrm{Pow}((p_i,r_i),(p_j,r_j)) - \varepsilon(r_i+r_j)^2 \le \mathrm{Pow}((f(p_i),r_i),(f(p_j),r_j)) \le (1+\varepsilon)\mathrm{Pow}((p_i,r_i),(p_j,r_j)) + \varepsilon(r_i+r_j)^2$.
conclusions: $\exists f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^m$, $m=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$, with the stated multiplicative-plus-additive bounds on $\mathrm{Pow}$

nodes.name: Power-distance JL Lemma (Theorem 3.3)
nodes.statement: Given any $n\times n$ symmetric hollow $D$ with power-distance representation $\{(p_i,r)\}$, $r=\sqrt{|e_n|}/2$, $e_n$ the smallest eigenvalue of $\mathrm{Gram}(D)=-\tfrac{1}{2}CDC$, there exists $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$ with $m=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ such that $(1-\varepsilon)\mathrm{Pow}((p_i,r),(p_j,r)) - 4\varepsilon r^2 \le \mathrm{Pow}((f(p_i),r),(f(p_j),r)) \le (1+\varepsilon)\mathrm{Pow}((p_i,r),(p_j,r)) + 4\varepsilon r^2$.
conclusions: $\exists f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, $m=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$, achieving $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ multiplicative and $4\varepsilon r^2$ additive distortion of pairwise power distances

nodes.name: Casey's theorem for generalized power distance
nodes.statement: If four circles in the plane are tangent to a fifth circle, then their pairwise generalized power distances $P_{ij}$, $i,j\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, satisfy the Ptolemy identity $P_{12}P_{34} + P_{23}P_{41} = P_{13}P_{24}$.

nodes.name: Optimality lower bound on JL target dimension
nodes.statement: Any dimension reduction algorithm achieving the JL distortion guarantee requires target dimension $\Omega(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$; this lower bound transfers to power-distance JL via the same argument.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Apply standard JL separately on $\{x_i^{(p)}\}$ and $\{x_i^{(q)}\}$, then combine via the diagonal block projection $f(x)=(f_p(x^{(p)}),f_q(x^{(q)}))$ and bound $\|f(x_i)-f(x_j)\|_{p',q'}^2$ using the $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ Euclidean bounds.

nodes.name: Apply standard JL on $p$-part and $q$-part
nodes.statement: By the standard JL lemma (Eq.\,1) there exist $f_p:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^{p'}$ and $f_q:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}^{q'}$ with $p',q'=O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ giving $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ Euclidean preservation on $\{x_i^{(p)}\}$ and $\{x_i^{(q)}\}$.

nodes.name: Combine to bound $(p',q')$-norm of difference
nodes.statement: Using $\|f(x_i)-f(x_j)\|_{p',q'}^2 = \|f_p(\cdot)\|_E^2 - \|f_q(\cdot)\|_E^2$ and the upper / lower bounds from step 1 yields $\|f(x_i)-f(x_j)\|_{p',q'}^2 \le \|x_i-x_j\|_{p,q}^2 + \varepsilon \|x_i-x_j\|_E^2$; the lower bound is symmetric.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: Use the Central Limit Theorem on $\|v\|_E^2/(p+q)$ and $\|v\|_{p,q}^2/(p+q)$, which converge to $\mu$ and $\tfrac{p-q}{p+q}\mu$; substituting the conditions on $p,q$ yields the claimed bounds.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.6
nodes.statement: Express the uniform sphere distribution in terms of i.i.d. Gaussians $Y_i$, apply chi-square concentration to $\sum Y_i^2$ and to $\sum_{i\le p} Y_i^2 - \sum_{i>p} Y_i^2$, set $\delta=\varepsilon/(4C+2+\varepsilon C)$ to obtain $\|u-v\|_E/\|u-v\|_{p,q} \le C(1+\varepsilon/2)$ w.h.p., then plug into Theorem/Lemma 2.2 with parameter $\varepsilon/(2C)$.

nodes.name: Express uniform sphere as normalized Gaussians
nodes.statement: Write $Y = (Y_1,\dots,Y_{p+q})/\sqrt{\sum_i Y_i^2}$ with $Y_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$ to represent the uniform distribution on $S^{p+q-1}$.

nodes.name: Chi-square concentration on numerator and denominator
nodes.statement: Apply $P(\chi^2 \in (1\pm\delta)(p+q)) \ge 1-2e^{-\frac{p+q}{2}(\frac{1}{2}\delta^2 - \frac{1}{3}\delta^3)}$ to both $\sum_i Y_i^2$ and $\sum_{i\le p} Y_i^2 - \sum_{i>p} Y_i^2$.

nodes.name: Choose $\delta$ and bound the ratio
nodes.statement: Setting $\delta=\varepsilon/(4C+2+\varepsilon C)$ and using a union bound, w.h.p. $\|u-v\|_E/\|u-v\|_{p,q} \le C(1+\varepsilon/2)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.2 with adjusted $\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Invoke Lemma 2.2 with parameter $\varepsilon/(2C)$ and combine with the ratio bound to conclude $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ multiplicative distortion of $\|\cdot\|_{p,q}^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathrm{Gram}(E) = -\tfrac{1}{2}CEC = -\tfrac{1}{2}CDC + 2r^2 C$ using $C(I-J)=C$ and $C^2=C$. Since $C$ is PSD with eigenvalue $0$ on $\mathbf{1}_n$ and $1$ elsewhere, eigenvalues of $\mathrm{Gram}(E)$ equal those of $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$ shifted by $2r^2$; PSD iff $2r^2 \ge |e_n|$.

nodes.name: Compute Gram matrix of $E$
nodes.statement: $-\tfrac{1}{2}CEC = -\tfrac{1}{2}C(D-4r^2(I-J))C = -\tfrac{1}{2}CDC + 2r^2 C(I-J)C = -\tfrac{1}{2}CDC + 2r^2 C$, using $C(I-J)=C$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue analysis via centering matrix
nodes.statement: $C$ has eigenvalue $0$ on $\mathbf{1}_n$ and $1$ elsewhere; therefore $\mathrm{Gram}(E)$ has the same kernel direction as $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$ and remaining eigenvalues equal to those of $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$ plus $2r^2$.

nodes.name: Conclude PSD condition
nodes.statement: All eigenvalues of $\mathrm{Gram}(E)$ are $\ge 0$ iff $2r^2 \ge |e_n|$, the absolute value of the smallest eigenvalue of $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: Apply standard JL to the centers $\{p_i\}$ to get $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ approximation of $\|p_i-p_j\|_E^2$, then subtract $(r_i+r_j)^2$ on both sides and rearrange to obtain the additive $\varepsilon(r_i+r_j)^2$ error on $\mathrm{Pow}$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-Euclidean JL Transform
nodes.statement: Compute pseudo-Euclidean coordinates of dissimilarity matrix $D$ via spectral decomposition, then run two standard JL transforms on the $p$-part and $q$-part.

nodes.name: Orthogonal decomposition of $D$
nodes.statement: Find $D = O\Lambda O^T$ where $\Lambda$ is the diagonal matrix of eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Set $(p,q)$ signature $A = \mathrm{sign}(\Lambda)$
nodes.statement: Let $A = \mathrm{sign}(\Lambda)$ to identify the signature of the bilinear form.

nodes.name: Embed into $\mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ via $V A V^T$
nodes.statement: Compute the embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{p,q}$ as $V A V^T$.

nodes.name: Split each $x$ into $x^{(p)},x^{(q)}$ and apply standard JL to each part
nodes.statement: For each embedded point $x$, split into $x^{(p)}$ and $x^{(q)}$ and apply standard JL projections to $\mathbb{R}^{p'}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{q'}$ respectively, with $p',q'$ the target dimensions.

nodes.name: Return projected points and signature
nodes.statement: Return the projected points $(x^{(p')},x^{(q')})$ together with the signature $(p',q')$.

nodes.name: Power Distance JL Transform
nodes.statement: Convert dissimilarity matrix $D$ into a Euclidean distance matrix by adding $4r^2(J-I)$ for $r=\sqrt{|e_n|}/2$, recover Euclidean coordinates, then apply standard JL.
output: Projected centers in $\mathbb{R}^m$ with $m = O(\log n/\varepsilon^2)$

nodes.name: Orthogonal decomposition $D = O\Lambda O^T$
nodes.statement: Find the orthogonal decomposition of the dissimilarity matrix $D = O\Lambda O^T$.

nodes.name: Compute $r = \sqrt{|e_n|}/2$ from smallest eigenvalue of $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$
nodes.statement: Let $e_n$ be the smallest eigenvalue of $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$ and set $r = \sqrt{|e_n|}/2$.

nodes.name: Form Euclidean matrix $E = D + 4r^2(J-I)$
nodes.statement: Add $4r^2(J-I)$ to $D$ to obtain Euclidean distance matrix $E$.

nodes.name: Recover coordinates $X'$ and apply standard JL
nodes.statement: Recover Euclidean coordinates $X'$ such that $E_{ij} = \|x'_i-x'_j\|^2$ and apply standard JL to target dimension $m$.

nodes.name: Return projected points with radii $r$
nodes.statement: Return the projected points along with their (common) radius $r$.

nodes.name: Non-Euclidean dimensionality reduction from a dissimilarity matrix
nodes.statement: Given an $n\times n$ symmetric hollow (possibly non-metric) dissimilarity matrix $D$, produce a low-dimensional embedding of the underlying $n$ items that approximately preserves all pairwise dissimilarities.

nodes.name: Random-simplex synthetic dataset
nodes.statement: Each of $n$ points has its first $n-1$ coordinates form a simplex while the final coordinate dominates pairwise distances, producing a single very large negative eigenvalue in $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$.

nodes.name: Euclidean-ball synthetic dataset
nodes.statement: $n$ balls with varying radii whose dissimilarity is the minimum surface-to-surface distance, yielding dissimilarities that violate the triangle inequality (inspired by Delft's balls [DP10]).

nodes.name: CuMiDa genomics datasets (Brain, Breast, Renal)
nodes.statement: Three cancer-related microarray datasets from CuMiDa with dissimilarities computed via entropic affinity.

nodes.name: MNIST and CIFAR-10 image datasets
nodes.statement: 1000 randomly sampled images each from MNIST and CIFAR-10 with $k$-nearest-neighbor (Isomap, $k=10$) dissimilarities.

nodes.name: SNAP graph datasets (Email-Eu-core, Facebook ego-networks, MOOC-actions)
nodes.statement: Real-world unweighted undirected graphs from the SNAP collection with shortest-path distances as dissimilarities.

nodes.name: $k$-means clustering downstream task
nodes.statement: Apply the proposed JL transforms to reduce dimension and then run $k$-means; compare clustering cost to the original optimum on Brain, Breast, Email, and Facebook datasets.

nodes.name: Connection to Lorentzian / Minkowski space
nodes.statement: The $(n-1,1)$ signature is exactly the Lorentzian inner product; 4-dimensional Lorentzian space is Minkowski space (special relativity), and the unit hyperboloid in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with imaginary Lorentzian length is the hyperboloid model of $\mathbb{H}^n$.

nodes.name: Implementing $f$ via block-diagonal random matrix
nodes.statement: If $f_p, f_q$ are realized by random matrices $M_{p'p}, M_{q'q}$, then $f$ is the block-diagonal matrix $M$ of dimension $(p'+q')\times(p+q)$ with $M_p,M_q$ on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere; $f(x)=Mx$.

nodes.name: Statistical interpretation as silhouette of Gaussians
nodes.statement: Theorem 3.1 implies any symmetric hollow $D$ is the silhouette-coefficient matrix of $n$ Gaussian distributions centered at $\{p_i\}$ with common variance $r$, linking non-Euclidean dissimilarities to measurement uncertainty.

nodes.name: Computational efficiency via SVD on Gram matrix
nodes.statement: Recovery of coordinates from $D$ uses SVD on $\mathrm{Gram}(D)$ in $O(n^3)$ time; landmark MDS or appending the $4r^2$ correction directly can speed this up; if coordinates come from representation learning, this step is skipped.

nodes.name: $(p,q)$ bilinear form
nodes.statement: $\langle u,v\rangle = \sum_{i=1}^p u_i v_i - \sum_{i=p+1}^{p+q} u_i v_i = u^T \Lambda v$.

nodes.name: Coordinate recovery from Gram decomposition
nodes.statement: $X = (x_1,\dots,x_n) = \mathrm{Diag}(\sqrt{|\lambda_1|},\dots,\sqrt{|\lambda_n|})\cdot U^T$, giving $D_{ij} = (x_i-x_j)^T \Lambda (x_i-x_j)$.

nodes.name: Silhouette score equals generalized power distance (Eq. 12)
nodes.statement: $SC_W(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y}) = \|\mu_x - \mu_y\|^2 - (\sigma_x+\sigma_y)^2$.
